RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Morgan Iverson
Member ID: W192391130
Reference Number: POC-D5B17E1A47-69764
Date of Notice: 2026-08-25
Requested Service/CPT: Partial (unicompartmental) knee replacement, CPT 27446
Treating Surgeon: [Duval, MD] — Orthopedic Surgery

To the Wellpoint Appeals Review Team:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 27446 (partial knee replacement), dated 2026-08-25. This appeal is timely: the notice states that an appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by 2027-02-21, and this letter is being submitted well within that window.

1. Stated reason for denial

The notice states that the request is denied because "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I respectfully disagree, and the clinical record summarized below documents a conservative treatment trial that is substantial in both duration and modality.

2. The Carelon Medical Benefits Management "Joint Surgery" Clinical Appropriateness Guideline

Wellpoint's own provider communications identify Carelon Medical Benefits Management, Inc. as the vendor that reviews joint-surgery prior authorization requests, applying its "Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines... Musculoskeletal Appropriate Use Criteria: Joint Surgery," which includes a dedicated "Knee Arthroplasty (Total/Partial/Revision Knee Replacement)" section covering CPT 27446. The version of this guideline in effect on the date of this denial is identified on its face as:

"Status: Revised Effective Date: 11/15/2025 Doc ID: MSK02-1125.1 Last Review Date: 04/21/2025"

I have not been able to obtain the verbatim text of the "Knee Arthroplasty" clinical-indications subsection of this specific document, and I am not quoting or attributing any knee-specific numeric threshold to Wellpoint or Carelon that I have not actually seen in that section. I am formally requesting, as part of this appeal, that Wellpoint provide me and Dr. Duval with a full copy of the "Knee Arthroplasty" section of Doc ID MSK02-1125.1 (effective 11/15/2025), including the specific criteria applied to this request, as I am entitled to under the plan's claims and appeals procedures and applicable state and federal law.

What I can document from the guideline itself is its general "Clinical Appropriateness Framework," which applies to all interventions reviewed under this guideline, including knee arthroplasty:

"Prior to any intervention, it is essential that the clinician confirms the diagnosis or establishes its pretest likelihood based on a complete evaluation of the patient. This includes a history and physical examination and, where applicable, a review of relevant laboratory studies, diagnostic testing, and response to prior therapeutic intervention... Providers may be required to submit clinical documentation in support of a request for services. Such documentation must a) accurately reflect the clinical situation at the time of the requested service, and b) sufficiently document the ordering provider's clinical intent."

I have also seen — in the Hip Arthroplasty section of this same current (11/15/2025) Carelon guideline document — a conservative-care requirement stated as follows. I am not asserting that this exact hip-section language governs the knee arthroplasty request; I present it only because it illustrates the general pattern Carelon uses across joint-arthroplasty indications in this current document (a defined conservative-care duration, waived when severe imaging findings are present):

"Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-surgical conservative management (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4, modified Outerbridge grade 4, or Tonnis grade 3)"

For additional historical context only — and explicitly not as a statement of the criteria currently in effect, since this text comes from an archived, superseded 2021–2022 edition of the same Carelon "Joint Surgery" guideline — that older edition's Knee Arthroplasty section stated the unicompartmental/partial knee arthroplasty conservative-care requirement as:

"Failure of at least 3 months of non-surgical conservative therapy (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4)... Elective medial or lateral unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA)/partial knee replacement (PKA) may be considered medically necessary when ALL of the following requirements are met."

I cite this superseded language only to show that, across every version of this guideline that I have been able to examine, Carelon has consistently (a) required a defined period of non-surgical conservative treatment, and (b) waived or reduced that requirement when imaging shows Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 (bone-on-bone) disease. Both the general "confirm the diagnosis... response to prior therapeutic intervention" language in the current 2025-11-15 edition and this consistent historical pattern support the position that the documentation submitted for Ms./Mr. Iverson meets the intent of the conservative-treatment requirement, regardless of which specific numeric threshold is ultimately confirmed in the current Knee Arthroplasty subsection.

3. The clinical record documents an adequate, and in fact severity-adjusted, conservative treatment trial

The following clinical facts, all documented in the prior authorization packet already submitted to Wellpoint, directly respond to the stated denial reason:

- Symptom duration: 14 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest, reflecting a chronic and worsening condition rather than an acute presentation for which surgery would be premature.
- Structured physical therapy: A supervised course of physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, spanning 12 weeks (2026-04-22 through 2026-07-15), with 20 completed visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- Pharmacologic management: NSAID therapy for 6 months with inadequate relief.
- Injection therapy: A corticosteroid injection administered 2026-05-01, which provided only 4 weeks of partial relief before symptoms returned.
- Imaging severity: MRI of the knee dated 2026-07-10 shows full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes medially — the same severe imaging finding that, in every version of the Carelon Joint Surgery guideline I have reviewed (both the current 2025-11-15 edition's parallel Hip Arthroplasty provision and the archived 2021–2022 Knee Arthroplasty provision), is treated as a basis for waiving or reducing the standard conservative-treatment duration requirement.
- Functional impairment: The patient cannot climb stairs without assistance and wakes 3–4 times nightly due to pain, demonstrating a significant, activity-limiting functional deficit.
- Physical exam: Positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain, corroborating the imaging and functional findings.
- No contraindications: There is no active infection and no untreated substance use disorder; the patient's BMI is 29 (not a disqualifying value under standard arthroplasty criteria), and the patient is a non-smoker.

Taken together, this record documents 6 months of NSAID therapy, a full 12-week/20-visit supervised physical therapy program, and a corticosteroid injection — a multi-modal conservative treatment trial — in a patient with 14 months of symptoms, bone-on-bone Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medial compartment disease on MRI, and significant functional impairment. This is precisely the clinical picture that, under the pattern found in every version of the applicable Carelon guideline I have reviewed, either satisfies or substantially exceeds the conservative-care requirement, particularly given the severe (grade 4) imaging findings that these guidelines recognize as a basis to waive or shorten the standard conservative-care duration.

4. Requested action

I ask that Wellpoint:

1. Reverse the denial of CPT 27446 and authorize the requested partial (unicompartmental) knee replacement; or, in the alternative,
2. Provide, in writing, the exact "Knee Arthroplasty" clinical-indications criteria from the current Carelon Joint Surgery guideline (Doc ID MSK02-1125.1, effective 11/15/2025) that were applied to this request, specifically identifying which criterion the submitted records are alleged not to satisfy, so that Dr. Duval and I can respond directly to that specific requirement; and
3. Arrange a peer-to-peer conversation between Dr. Duval and the reviewing physician, consistent with the guideline's own statement that "the determination of appropriateness will most likely require a peer-to-peer conversation" when documentation elements are contested.

I am enclosing/have previously submitted the physical therapy discharge note, medication and injection records, the 2026-07-10 MRI report, and the operative surgeon's clinical notes documenting exam findings and functional limitations in support of this appeal.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide written notice of the outcome within the timeframe required under the plan and applicable New Jersey and federal regulations. If this internal appeal is not resolved in the patient's favor, I reserve the right to pursue external review through New Jersey's Independent Health Care Appeals Program (IHCAP), administered by Maximus Federal Services, consistent with N.J.A.C. 11:24-1.2 and 11:24A-1.2.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Morgan Iverson
